question: Is our fair line better than the market, or merely a noisier copy of it?
known: Market closing line vs actual margin r=-0.439 (n=136). Our fair line vs actual margin r=-0.2227 (n=120). Mean absolute fair-vs-market gap 3.408 points (n=120).
missing: No season with more than nine weeks of games, so the sampling error on both coefficients is wider than their difference.
blocks: Promoting any side strategy, and trusting any edge number on the side.
closes_with: Grade a full season walk-forward and compare the two coefficients on the same games with a paired test, not two separate intervals.

question: Why does our total point the wrong way against outcomes?
known: Market total vs actual total r=0.3771 (n=136). Our fair total vs actual total r=-0.0418 (n=120), which has the wrong sign for the stated convention. Our totals also run 3.237 points above market on average.
missing: Whether the bias is one systematic term (the home-field prior added to both sides of the total) or genuine noise. Settling it needs a held-out season.
blocks: Every total strategy, including the ones that currently look positive.
closes_with: Refit the total without the duplicated home-field term on a held-out window and compare; do not refit on the graded weeks, which would be the overfit this project is built to avoid.
status: open - the bias is measured, not explained

question: Do we have permission to publish derived prices and to keep collecting?
known: The earlier session recorded NFL.com terms restrictions; this capture adds a second publisher (Sports Reference) whose historical line data it credits to Sports Odds History.
missing: No written permission from either publisher. No legal review. No statement of which of the two governs a derived number.
blocks: Publishing anything that looks like an executable price, releasing a dataset, and any scheduled retrieval.
closes_with: Read both publishers' terms line by line, record the exact clauses with links, and get a written answer if publication is intended.

question: Where is the opening number, and is the published number an open or a close?
known: The publisher prints exactly one number per game and does not label it open or close. It is recorded here as a closing snapshot. No opening number exists in the store.
missing: An official, retrievable archive of opening numbers for these games. ESPN shows a live open/current pair for the unplayed slate only; its completed-game pages render neither.
blocks: Any closing-line-value calculation, and any claim about line movement.
closes_with: Capture the open/current pair at a fixed timestamp before kickoff in future weeks, with the timestamp stored beside the number.

question: What vig, limit and liquidity does the reference price actually carry?
known: Spread and total are published. No price, hold percentage or limit is.
missing: A published moneyline or price for the spread and total, so the hold cannot be derived. Every staking figure here is at a stated assumed -110.
blocks: Any ROI, expected-value or break-even claim that depends on a real price.
closes_with: A source that publishes both sides of each market with prices, for enough games to estimate the hold.

question: Are two legs of a same-game parlay dependent, and by how much?
known: Home-cover vs over on the published numbers: phi=-0.1741 (n=126). Player-prop pairs are blank.
missing: Any published player price, so the dependence between two player props cannot be measured from official numbers.
blocks: Pricing any same-game combination without assuming independence.
closes_with: A licensed player-price feed, then a joint-frequency estimate with n.

question: Does losing a starter matter more when the position is printed two deep?
known: 265 injury rows matched to a printed chart; 65 have no printed name behind the replacement. Offence and defence are counted separately (127 offence, 126 defence).
missing: Only one week of depth charts exists, so there is no variation in depth to fit against outcomes. Sixty-one injury rows match no printed slot.
blocks: Any injury coefficient, and therefore any line adjustment for availability.
closes_with: Capture a chart every week for a full season, then test whether the depth measure predicts the residual against the closing line.

question: Is the depth data complete, given that it arrives in two separate files?
known: Two slot files with no overlap: one holds 27 clubs, the other holds the four Week-10 bye clubs. Combined, 31 clubs and 1817 printed slots. Houston publishes a chart that renders as an image and could not be read.
missing: One club with no readable printed chart, and any week before Week 10.
blocks: A complete league view of replacement depth.
closes_with: A readable Houston chart, and weekly capture going forward. Reading only the first file silently drops four clubs, which is recorded as PD01.

question: How many games would it take before a real edge could be seen at all?
known: At 80% power and a 5% two-sided test: 153 settled selections at a 60% true rate, 617 at 55%, 2,682 at 52.4%. The store holds 136 games.
missing: Nothing on the arithmetic. What is missing is the games.
blocks: Any promotion. Nothing in this snapshot can clear its own sample requirement.
closes_with: Accumulate settled selections to the stated threshold before ranking.

question: Do two clubs' pages ever disagree about the same game?
known: 136/136 games agree on the mirrored spread and 136/136 on the total. 272 publisher verdicts were re-derived with zero mismatches.
missing: Agreement between two pages of the same publisher is not independent verification. No second, independent price source has been read.
blocks: A claim of external verification. The store is single-publisher.
closes_with: Read one independent price source and record every disagreement.

question: Should a strategy that ranks now be trusted next week?
known: The demotion gate (DG01) is written and applied: 8 of 12 variants sit in demote_to_paper, 0 rank. Nothing has passed it.
missing: No live strategy exists to demote, so the gate has only ever fired on paper. Its first live test is untested.
blocks: Any claim that the gate works in production.
closes_with: Run the gate across several seasons in replay and record how often it fires correctly and how often it demotes a strategy that later recovered.

question: Is the model's better-looking side result skill or selection?
known: 11 variants clear the selection floor and none clears multiplicity control at q<=0.1. The best signal hit rate is 0.5763 on n=59.
missing: The variants were chosen after seeing the data. Even with the correction, the family itself is not a pre-registered one.
blocks: Treating any of these twelve as a finding rather than a screening pass.
closes_with: Freeze the family, then test on a future window that did not exist when the family was written.
